account:
Today I have been following my appointments, though running late, and trying to establish whether there is anything behind a story about changes to the bridge or port. I am now at the neighbour's east-bank cottage for tea, with my 16:30 office appointment approaching. The neighbour welcomed me but has not yet answered my direct question about what they personally heard at the bakery.

So far I have no verified evidence of a crossing change or secret undertaking. The secretary reports that the baker described ordinary freight business and had no firsthand evidence of crossing changes. Neither could identify the mill keeper. At my morning grain inspection I saw 128 hay bales for sale, but did not inspect storage or deliveries or meet a responsible keeper. That leaves the inspection incomplete; it does not itself demonstrate anything improper.

There are a few observations worth following up. Yesterday I saw freight give the secretary a written book. Today a towns-person said freight was carrying a sack of bread at the inn, and another said the baker was carrying wheat at the bakery. Those reports fit food supply and delivery work, but I do not know the freight book's contents or the purpose and destination of the bread. I should ask rather than connect these facts into an unsupported story.

The builder reports no specific visible defects on the bridge and public lighting routes, no expenditure, and no proposed charges. His work was only a visual inspection, not a structural survey or nighttime lighting test. I supplied the secretary with two emeralds for writing books so these limits and findings can be recorded. Council letters have not yet been identified or presented to me. I saw the secretary take a written book from the office chest this afternoon, but do not know which book it was.

My present impression is that ordinary town business is continuing, while my information about freight, the mill, and the alleged crossing discussion is incomplete. The neighbour may be able to identify the original words and speaker. Until then I cannot responsibly say who is arranging anything unusual or what it is for.
